rows.question: My cat keeps sneezing and has watery eyes
rows.reply:
Sneezing that keeps going and running a runny nose are common signs of an upper respiratory infection, often called cat flu. Viruses like feline herpesvirus and calicivirus are common causes, and they spread easily between cats. Other signs include a cough, a runny nose, mouth sores, tiredness and poor appetite.

What helps:
- Gently wipe your cat's nose clean. A blocked nose can stop a cat smelling food, so it may eat less.
- Make sure your cat keeps eating and drinking.

Go to the vet immediately if the sneezing doesn't stop. Go to the vet also if your cat:
- Has trouble breathing, or the gums look bluish
- Haven't eaten properly for 24 hours
- Is a kitten. Young cats are more likely to get seriously ill.

rows.question: What should I feed my cat?
rows.reply: Once or twice a day for most cats. Leave food out all day for some cats, but make sure there is enough to eat. If you can't feel the ribs without pressing hard, there is too much fat, so ask your vet how much to cut back.

rows.question: Does my cat need vaccines if she never goes outside?
rows.reply:
Yes, usually at an early age. Core vaccines for cats cover three of the four core vaccines given to dogs: panleukopenia, herpesvirus and calicivirus; Rabies and FeLV when present or required by law; and FVRCP up to date. Good news: global guidelines say low-risk indoor cats usually need core boosters only every 3 years or longer.

Ask your vet about other vaccines you may already have, and follow their after-care advice.

rows.question: Is chocolate bad for cats?
rows.reply:
Yes. Chocolate is on the list of common poisons, along with coffee and energy drinks, grapes and raisins, onions and garlic, xylitol, human painkillers, paracetamol (for dogs) and ibuprofen. It also harms cats.

Act fast, even if your cat seems fine. Signs can take hours or days.

What to do now:
- Move your cat away from the source and remove anything left in their mouth, if it's safe to do so.
- Note what they ate, about how much, and when. Bring the packaging or label.
- Call your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now and tell them you're on your way.
- Wash with mild dish soap and lukewarm water, then rinse well.

Don't:
- Make your cat vomit unless a vet tells you to. It's dangerous with some poisons and if your pet is drowsy.
- Use home remedies like salt, milk, oil or hydrogen peroxide.
- Give any human medicine.

Go to a vet now.

rows.question: How many times a day should I feed an adult dog?
rows.reply:
Most adult dogs do well on 1 or 2 meals a day. The ASPCA suggests two meals, about 8 to 12 hours apart.

If you decide to give your dog more than one meal a day, ask your vet how much to cut back. Always keep fresh, clean water out.

rows.question: My dog has been vomiting since this morning
rows.reply:
One vomit in a dog that otherwise seems well is often not serious, and many cases settle within a day. But vomiting can also be a sign of poisoning, a blockage or other illness.

Go to the vet right away if your dog vomits and also has:
- Blood in the vomit
- Diarrhea, belly pain or fever
- Low energy, no appetite or signs of dehydration
- A chance of having swallowed something toxic or an object

See your vet today if vomiting goes on for more than 24 hours, even if your dog seems fine. Also ask your vet to keep a vomiting record, including when it started and how long it lasted.

rows.question: Can I give my dog aspirin?
rows.reply:
Go to your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now. Aspirin (naproxen and aspirin (NSAIDs) ) is on the list of medicines to which humans must be alert, and aspirin (NSAIDs) is human pain reliever on the list of drugs to which humans need to be alert. They can cause stomach ulcers, bleeding and kidney damage, and large amounts can cause seizures or coma.

If your dog does swallow it:
- Go to the vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now. Signs may include vomiting, diarrhea, black stools, belly pain, not eating, weakness and pale gums.
- Only make your dog vomit if a vet tells you to.
- Don't give any other medicine.

Before you go:
- Bring the bottle and count how many tablets are missing, so the vet can judge the risk.
- Only give it to your vet, so ask them to describe it to you first.

On the way, keep your dog calm and watch for vomiting or weakness. Never give human pain medicine to a dog without your vet's advice.

rows.question: My dog is having a seizure
rows.reply:
Stay calm and focus on keeping him safe while it happens:

- While it's happening, move furniture and hard objects away. Only move him if he's near stairs, water or another danger.
- Keep your hands away from his mouth. He can't control his jaws and may bite without meaning to.
- Don't try to hold him down.
- Time the seizure, and take a short video for the vet if you can.

Go to your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now if the seizure lasts more than about 3 minutes, if there's more than one in a row, or if he might have eaten something poisonous. Otherwise, call your vet soon after.

Afterward he may pace or seem confused. On the way to the vet, keep him calm, quiet and away from edges.

rows.question: Is tick fever common in the Philippines?
rows.reply:
Yes. It's one of the main reasons pets need a vet now: "tick fever" usually means germs like Ehrlichia, Anaplasma or Babesia spread by ticks. The warm climate in the Philippines suits the brown dog tick, which can live in homes and kennels. Ehrlichia canis was the most common tick-borne germ found in a study of dogs in Metro Manila and Laguna.

Signs may show 1 to 3 weeks after a bite:
- Fever, low energy, poor appetite
- Swelling of the glands, stiffness or limping
- Nosebleeds, bruises on the skin or gums, or blood in urine or poop

See a vet today if you notice bleeding, bruising, pale gums or weakness. A blood test is needed to confirm it. Prevent it with year-round tick control your vet recommends and daily tick checks.

rows.question: Is there a penalty for animal cruelty here?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under Section 9 of the Animal Welfare Act, as amended by RA 10631, the following penalties apply:
- Animal dies: 1 year, 6 months and 1 day to 2 years in prison, and/or a fine up to P100,000
- Animal survives but is severely injured and can't survive without human help: 1 year and 1 day to 1 year and 6 months, and/or up to P50,000
- Other cruelty or neglect: 6 months to 1 year, and/or up to P30,000

Penalties go up to 2 years and 1 day to 3 years and/or up to P250,000 if the offense involves a syndicate, a business, a public officer, or 3 or more animals.

There is no specified penalty for abandoning a pet without arranging its care.

rows.question: How do I stop my cat scratching the sofa?
rows.reply:
Scratching is normal for cats. It keeps their claws healthy and marks their space, so give them a better place to do it:
- Put a sturdy scratching post next to the sofa, tall enough for a full stretch.
- Try both upright posts and flat cardboard scratchers.
- Reward your cat with treats or play when they use it.
- Cover the sofa spots with a throw or double-sided tape for a while.
- Trim the claws regularly.

Don't punish or declaw your cat.

rows.question: What vaccines does my kitten need?
rows.reply:
Most kittens get these core vaccines:
- FVRCP (cat flu and panleukopenia), usually starting at 6 to 8 weeks and repeated every 3 to 4 weeks until about 16 weeks
- Rabies, given from around 12 weeks, which is required in the Philippines

Your vet may also suggest FeLV if your kitten will go outdoors or live with other cats. Keep the vaccine card with your pet and add each shot in FurFriends so you get reminders for boosters.

rows.question: Nagsusuka ang pusa ko kanina pa
rows.reply:
Go to the vet now. Repeated vomiting, going without bathroom breaks, or having blood in the vomit or stool need a vet right away. One episode in a bright adult pet is often minor, but call your vet and describe what you've seen at the same time.

What to do now:
- Call your vet and describe what you've seen. A photo helps.
- Offer small amounts of water often.
- If your vet agrees, feed small portions of bland food, like plain boiled chicken and rice for dogs.
- Keep a sick puppy away from other dogs and disinfect the area. Parvovirus spread easily.

Don't:
- Give human anti-diarrhea or stomach medicines. Some are toxic to cats and some dogs.
- Withhold food from a cat for more than a day. It can cause liver disease.

Go to the vet now.

rows.question: When does my puppy need the anti-rabies shot?
rows.reply:
Your puppy usually gets one at about 3 months old, then another as your vet advises, usually every year. In the Philippines, the Anti-Rabies Act requires dogs to be vaccinated against rabies.

- Many LGUs hold free anti-rabies vaccination drives, so ask your barangay or city vet.
- Keep the vaccination card, because you may need it for travel or boarding.
- Also get the core puppy shots, which your vet will schedule.

rows.question: My dog has a small cut on his paw, what do I do?
rows.reply:
Keep him calm and limit activity. Gently check the paw for cuts, a broken nail, or something stuck between the toes. If there's no wound yet:
- Stop if your dog shows pain: dogs in pain may bite, even their owners.
- Don't give human pain medicines unless your vet tells you to. They can poison pets.

Go to the vet now if the paw looks bent or swollen, your dog can't stand or walk without help, was hit by a vehicle or attacked by another animal, or is in severe pain.

See your vet within 24 hours if the limp lasts more than a day or is getting worse.

rows.question: Why is my dog scratching so much?
rows.reply:
Scratching can be due to itching from an illness or a new place, scratching to get away from a bit of trouble, or scratching as a way of playing. Common places for scratching include the back of the neck, behind the ears, the chest and abdomen, the head and nose, the front of the body and the paws. Itching only in certain seasons often points to a seasonally relevant allergen.

Other reasons scratch too: to play, to lick the skin a lot, to bite or lick the skin, or to lick the back of the neck. Scratching in the backyard can be due to being chased by a dog or a cat.

If your dog seems unwell or in pain while scratching, ask your vet what might be causing it. Scratching can have other causes too, like mites or allergies to things like insect bites, food, pollen, mold or dust.

rows.question: My dog's belly is swollen and he keeps trying to vomit
rows.reply:
Go to the vet immediately. Swelling in the abdomen can be caused by bloat, which needs surgery right away. Bloat is when the stomach fills with gas and twists, and it can kill within hours.

Other symptoms include a swollen belly, drooling, pale gums, restlessness, pacing, being unable to get comfortable, and drooling, pale gums, collapse.

Go to the vet now. Call ahead so they can prepare, and keep your dog as calm and still as you can on the way. Don't wait to see if it passes, give food, water or home remedies, or try making them vomit.

rows.question: Ilang beses dapat paliguan ang aso?
rows.reply:
Dogs: At least once every three months. Dogs that spend a lot of time outdoors or have skin problems may need baths more often.

Cats: Most cats keep themselves clean. They only need a bath if they get very dirty or into something sticky or smelly.

Bath tips:
- Trim the claws first, and use a rubber mat so they don't slip.
- Brush out loose hair and mats first.
- Use lukewarm water and a shampoo made for pets. Human shampoo can irritate or dry out the skin.
- Keep water out of the eyes, ears and nose. Wipe the face with a damp cloth.

See your vet if you notice scabs, bald spots, redness or constant scratching.

rows.question: Nalalagas ang balahibo ng pusa ko
rows.reply:
Bald or thin patch on the neck is one sign of a collar that fits badly. Other signs include red, scaly, smelly or crusty skin, heavy scratching, licking or chewing, and hair loss that is sudden or spreading.

Other than shedding, normal shedding in cats includes thinning the coat evenly with no bald patches. Hair loss is a sign of another problem, not a disease on its own. Common causes in cats are fleas and flea allergy, other parasites, fungal or bacterial skin infections, allergies, and overgrooming from stress or pain. See your vet if you notice bald or thin patches, licking or scratching the same spot a lot, or licking or scratching an itchy or painful spot.

At the same time, keep a close eye on other changes, like weight loss, low energy or a change in eating or drinking.

rows.question: Nagtatae ang pusa ko ng dalawang araw na
rows.reply:
Mild diarrhea in an adult cat that is still bright and eating can sometimes be watched at home for a short time. Always keep fresh water out, because diarrhea can quickly cause dehydration.

At home:
- Always keep fresh water out. Diarrhea can quickly become dehydrated.
- Ask your vet about a short rest for the stomach, or small meals of a bland or gut-friendly diet.
- When the stool firms up, switch back to the usual food slowly over about a week.

See your vet if it lasts more than 24 hours. Go now if there is:
- Blood in the stool
- Vomiting
- Weakness, fever, belly pain or no appetite

Go now if your cat also had a toy, bone or poison. These can be on the list of things to keep an eye on when you go to the vet.

rows.question: Why does my dog eat grass?
rows.reply:

Things to watch:
- Keep your dog off treated lawns where grass is used as food.
- Grass can carry worm eggs from other animals' poop, so ask your vet about regular deworming.

See your vet if your dog eats grass and then vomits often or seems to have stomach pain. That can point to a stomach or gut problem that needs checking.

- Diarrhea, belly pain or fever
- Low energy, no appetite or signs of dehydration
- A chance of having swallowed something toxic or an object

See your vet today if vomiting goes on for more than 24 hours, even if your dog seems fine. Also ask your vet to keep a vomiting record, including when it started and how long it lasted.

rows.question: How do I get rid of fleas in my house?
rows.reply:
Most of the flea problem lives in your home, not on your pet. Eggs fall off into carpets, bedding and corners, and flea cocoons can wait there for months.

- Treat every dog and cat in the home, not just the itchy one, using products your vet recommends.
- Vacuum often.
- Wash pet bedding and blankets regularly.
- If you use a home spray, keep pets out of the room and follow the label.
- Never put a house or yard product directly on a pet.

Year-round flea prevention is advised, and it can take weeks to months of steady treatment to fully clear an infestation. Fleas can live indoors all year, so experts advise year-round flea prevention.

rows.question: What should I put in a pet first aid kit?
rows.reply:
Put some basic items in your pet's first aid kit, and one extra in case your pet loses it. It helps in the first minutes but never replaces a vet.

A basic kit includes:
- Gauze, sterile pads, stretch bandage and adhesive tape
- Small blunt-tipped scissors and tweezers
- Saline solution for rinsing wounds and eyes
- Cotton balls or swabs and disposable gloves
- A muzzle for dogs, and a towel for wrapping or carrying
- A rectal thermometer and lubricating jelly
- Splint material
- A small supply of your pet's regular medicines

Your kit should also include your vet's number, the nearest 24-hour clinic, and your pet's health records. Keep it in a box with a secure lid you can grab fast, and check expiry dates every year. Ask your vet before giving any medicine, and only make your pet vomit if a vet tells you to.

rows.question: Why is my dog scratching so much?
rows.reply:
Scratching can be due to itching from an illness, an allergy or both, being bitten by a tick, having a heavy flea load, or trying to get away. Itching all year can point to dust mites or food, and scratching in one place usually means scratching elsewhere.

Other reasons include:
- Bitten by a tick
- Licking or licking the skin a lot
- Licking or licking the head
- Licking or licking the tail
- Licking or licking the back of the neck
- Licking or licking the sides of the ears
- Licking or licking the paws
- Scratching in one spot
- Scratching anywhere

Look through the coat for fleas or flea dirt, and at the skin for redness, scabs or hair loss. Note where your dog scratches. Licking and rubbing of the feet and face is common with allergies and infections.

Itching alone or in one place usually means scratching elsewhere. Scratching everywhere usually means scratching elsewhere. Scratching in one spot usually means scratching elsewhere.

If your dog scratched last time and hasn't scratched yet, keep a scratch record.

rows.question: My dog has been vomiting since this morning
rows.reply:
One vomit in a dog that otherwise seems well is often not serious, and many cases settle within a day. But vomiting can also be a sign of poisoning, a blockage or other illness.

Go to the vet right away if your dog vomits and also has:
- Blood in the vomit
- Diarrhea, belly pain or fever
- Low energy, no appetite or signs of dehydration
- A chance of having swallowed something toxic or an object

See your vet today if vomiting goes on for more than 24 hours, even if your dog seems fine. Also ask your vet to keep a vomiting-free record, including when the last episode happened.

rows.question: My dog howls and barks when I go to work
rows.reply:
Barking while going to work can be due to anxiety or a new environment. It's often separation anxiety: your dog is stressed being alone.
- Give a good walk and play before you go.
- Practice short absences, then gradually make them longer.
- Keep leaving and coming home calmly and low-key.
- Don't punish the barking, because it adds to the stress.

If your dog also destroys things, soils the house or hurts themselves, talk to your vet or a trainer. Some dogs need a behavior plan.

rows.question: Is it required by law to vaccinate my dog against rabies in the Philippines?
rows.reply:
Yes. The Anti-Rabies Act requires dogs to be vaccinated against rabies, and many LGUs hold free anti-rabies vaccination drives. Ask your barangay or city vet about the schedule.

Keep the vaccination record on your dog's vaccination or registration card.

rows.question: Nagsusuka ang aso ko, ano ang dapat gawin?
rows.reply:
Bleeding in the stomach can be from blood in the stomach or gut, ulcers caused by human pain relievers, rat poison, or swallowed chemicals. Call your vet or the nearest 24-hour veterinary clinic now and go in, especially if your dog keeps vomiting, is weak, has pale gums or a painful belly.

If your dog also keeps throwing up or having seizures, go to a vet now. Bleeding in the stomach can lead to shock and death.

Go in even if your dog seems fine at first. Bleeding in the stomach can happen after vomiting or diarrhea started.

Also go in if your dog kept vomiting last time: call your vet and describe what you've seen. A photo helps.

rows.question: Can I give my dog aspirin?
rows.reply:
Go to your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now. Aspirin (naproxen and aspirin (NSAIDs) ) is on the list of medicines to avoid for dogs because they can cause stomach ulcers, bleeding and kidney damage, and large amounts can cause seizures or coma.

If your dog already took it, take it again. But only after asking your vet first. Go even if your pet seems fine at first.

rows.question: My dog is having a seizure
rows.reply:
Stay calm and focus on keeping him safe while it happens:

- While it's happening, move furniture and hard objects away. Only move him if he's near stairs, water or another danger.
- Keep your hands away from his mouth. He can't control his jaws and may bite without meaning to.
- Don't try to hold him down.
- Time the seizure, and take a short video for the vet if you can.

Go to your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now if the seizure lasts more than about 3 minutes, if there's more than one in a row, or if he might have eaten something poisonous. Otherwise, call your vet soon after.

Afterward he may pace or seem confused. On the way to the vet, keep him calm, quiet and away from edges.

rows.question: Why does my dog eat grass?
rows.reply:
Dogs may eat grass for fiber, out of boredom or to get attention, or simply from instinct. It is very common, and most grass-eating dogs are not sick. Fewer than 1 in 4 dogs vomit after eating grass.

If your dog may have eaten it, keep it off treated lawns and ask your vet about regular deworming. Also ask your vet about regular exercise, which can help prevent future problems.

See your vet if your dog eats grass and then vomits often or seems to have stomach pain. That can point to a stomach or gut problem that needs checking.

rows.question: Is there free anti-rabies vaccine for dogs in the Philippines?
rows.reply: Often, yes. Section 6 of RA 9482 tells the Department of Agriculture to lead free anti-rabies vaccination of dogs, with priority for high-risk, low-income areas. LGUs must fund vaccines and run registration and vaccination (Section 7).
